input_oneliner: Rapid page: 68F HTN, AF on apixaban, RN found L facial droop and slurred speech, last seen normal 40 min ago

reference_targets_freetext.item: Forehead sparing: ask the patient to raise eyebrows and close eyes tightly; compare upper versus lower face weakness
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Forehead sparing indicates an upper motor neuron (central) lesion; forehead involvement points to a peripheral facial nerve palsy

reference_targets_freetext.item: Pronator drift and arm and leg strength, gaze deviation, visual fields, and language testing (naming, repetition, comprehension)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Limb, gaze, field, or language deficits alongside facial droop establish a central lesion and drive stroke-alert activation

reference_targets_freetext.item: Establish last-known-well time precisely and ask about apixaban adherence and last dose
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Time window and anticoagulant status determine eligibility for reperfusion therapy

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about headache, neck pain, vomiting, and check blood pressure
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Severe headache and hypertension with a focal deficit raise concern for hemorrhage

reference_targets_freetext.item: Dysarthria versus aphasia: have the patient read a sentence and name objects
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Dysarthria alone is compatible with either central or peripheral lesion; aphasia is cortical

off_bedside_acceptable: Non-contrast CT head and CT angiography
should_not_recommend: Delaying stroke alert to complete a full neurologic examination
Prednisone for presumed Bell palsy without testing forehead sparing and limb strength
Antiplatelet or anticoagulant before imaging excludes hemorrhage

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: lower-face-only droop -> whole hemiface droop including forehead, eye will not close
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: Rapid page: 68F HTN, AF on apixaban, RN found L facial droop involving forehead and cannot close L eye, slurred speech, last seen normal 40 min ago
perturbation_pair.expected_change: Bell palsy rises to co-leading differential; forehead sparing check remains must-have; limb drift, gaze, and language testing remain but become confirmatory rather than the lead; otoscopy for ear canal vesicles and questions about ear pain, hyperacusis, and taste change rise.
